Sign in and out (President and Officer)\tready-for-agent, ticket\t2026-10-15T03:31:46Z\n1\tOPEN\tSpec: KCFC web CMS\tready-for-agent, spec\t2026-10-15T02:57:55Z\n---\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nProject vocabulary for the Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) website. One word per concept; if a better word appears, change it here.\n\n## People and roles\n\n**President**: One of the three students who run KCFC. Every President holds the Admin role.\n\n**Officer**: A club member other than a President who helps run the club. Every Officer holds the Editor role while in office.\n\n**Admin**: The role held by the three Presidents. Can create, edit, publish and delete Posts and Pages, and manage Users.\n\n**Editor**: The role held by Officers. Can create and edit Posts and save them as Drafts. Cannot publish, cannot delete a published Post, cannot touch Pages, and cannot see User management. An Editor sees and edits only their own Posts, so a sector team's writeup changes only through its own author until a President reviews it. Admins see and edit every Post.\n\n**User**: Anyone with an individual account on the admin console. Only Presidents and Officers are Users. Never shared between people.\n\n**Visitor**: Anyone reading the public site: prospective members, current members, alumni, recruiters. Visitors never log in, and everything on the public site is visible to all of them. There is no members-only content.\n\n**Sign-in**: A User signs in with their Kenyon email address and a password. A President creates the account and sets the first password face to face; there is no forced change at first sign-in. A lost password is reset by an Admin in person, never by email.\n\n**Idle sign-out**: A User is signed out automatically after about 2 hours without activity, because the Club laptop is shared at meetings.\n\n**Deactivated**: A User switched off by an Admin when their time in office ends. They can no longer sign in, and any open session ends at their next action. Their Posts keep their name as author. An Admin can reactivate them. Users are never deleted. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**: The one kind of dated club material: a meeting announcement, a pitch writeup, or an alumni call recap. There is a single kind of Post and no categories.\n\n**Pitch writeup**: A Post presenting a stock pitch. Spring pitches are group work by sector teams, so the team members are listed in the body text. It stays a Draft until a President has reviewed it.\n\n**Sector team**: One of the three groups in the spring stock pitch competition, each covering a sector and led by one President. Teams present to Kenyon alumni working in equity research at William Blair.\n\n**Analyst Program**: The club's program for newer members. Its lasting description is an Admin-only Page.\n\n**Page**: Lasting club information: About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join, Recruiting. Only Admins may create, edit or delete a Page; Editors cannot touch them at all.\n\n**Join Page**: The Page for prospective members: what the club does, whether prior experience is needed, how to come to a meeting.\n\n**Recruiting Page**: The Page for current members: the resume review form link and standing guides. Kept separate from the Join Page (one Page, one audience).\n\n**Homepage**: A Page edited by Admins. The next meeting (every other week, Oden 110) is the first thing a Visitor sees, followed by the contact email and the latest Posts.\n\n**Next-meeting line**: Plain text at the top of the Homepage, e.g. \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\". A President updates it the night before each meeting, the same habit as the email reminder. There is no calendar or automatic date logic.\n\n**Navigation**: The public menu. It lists Published Pages in an order an Admin sets, plus a link to the Posts listing.\n\n**Byline**: The public line on a Post, \"By <name>, <date>\", naming whoever posted it, never an email address. A Deactivated User's name still shows on their old Posts. Pages show no byline. Group work (such as the spring pitches by three sector teams, each led by a President) has no team field: the poster is the byline and the team members are listed in the body text.\n\n**Posts listing**: The public list of Published Posts, newest first, showing title and date.\n\n**Title convention**: A club habit, not enforced by the system: Post titles for pitches and recaps start with \"Pitch:\" or \"Recap:\" (e.g. \"Pitch: NVDA, Spring 2026\") so the Posts listing is scannable. Admins hand-link standout archive Posts from the Recruiting Page.\n\n**Event**: Not a separate thing. An event is announced in a Post.\n\n**Slug**: The short address-name of a Post or Page (e.g. `spring-stock-pitch`). Made from the title once, when first saved, and unchanged when the title is edited. Only an Admin can edit it; an old slug is not redirected.\n\n**Unpublish**: An Admin returns a Published Post or Page to Draft. It leaves the public site at the next Publish run but is kept.\n\n**Delete**: Permanent removal of a Post or Page, after an \"are you sure?\" step. Only an Admin can delete a Published Post or any Page; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Users are never deleted, only Deactivated (for example when seniors graduate in May: their old Posts keep their name, but they cannot log in).\n\n**Draft**: A Post that has been saved but not published. Visible only to signed-in Users, never on the public site. A Published Post returns to Draft when an Editor edits it, and stays out of the public site until an Admin publishes it again. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n\n**Published**: The status of a Post or Page that an Admin has approved for the public site. Approved is not the same as Live.\n\n**Publish run**: Running `cms publish`, which only an Admin does, usually right before a meeting. It rebuilds the public site from everything Published and deploys it, with no change summary. Marking an item Published has a simple \"Publish this?\" confirm on the button. A mistake is fixed by unpublishing it and running it again.\n\n**Live**: On the public site as of the last Publish run. A Published item becomes Live only at the next Publish run.\n\n**Pending changes**: Changes made since the last Publish run, which the console shows in a banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live.\n\n**Dashboard**: The console's first screen. Shows counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated Users), and a one-click \"New Post\" button.\n\n**Content list**: The console's list of Posts and Pages, newest first, filterable by status (with counts) and type. Editors see Posts only.\n\n**Preview**: The editor's side-by-side view of how the sanitized Markdown will look on the public site, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n\n**Club laptop**: The one computer that runs the admin console. The console is never on the public internet; Officers sign in on it with their own accounts.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nComments, image uploads, categories, scheduled posts, email newsletters, member logins.\nAGENTS.md\napp\nCLAUDE.md\nCONTEXT.md\ndata\ndev\ndocs\nnotes\npyproject.toml\nREADME.md\nscripts\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\nskills\nskills-lock.json\ntemplates\ntests\ntranscripts\nuv.lock\ne5ebe27 transcripts and ledger\n736a4f8 report notes, transcripts and ledger\n1dad7cf T01: usage ledger after code-review fixes\nb0d330b usage ledger\na34b666 skills: read and write CONTEXT.md, not GLOSSARY.md\nc6384e5 usage ledger\n1557b24 docs: the project glossary is CONTEXT.md, not GLOSSARY.md\n1a3a0e0 T01: refuse an unsafe CMS_SECRET_KEY in production\ne630ee8 T01: cleanups from code review\n31bc8c4 T01: sign in and out (President and Officer)\ncfa12d3 session transcripts and usage ledger\n717cc52 grill: CONTEXT.md and decisions\n84de25c exercise B: spend()\ne1b2777 token budget plan\n7446c85 setup: context-threshold warning hook\n02d5a20 field notes and client brief: Kenyon Finance Club Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n835299d remove template example transcripts\nf89c709 setup: template configured, T00 green\n0eb45ca Initial commit","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0da76dd6-8fb6-4462-b047-4119d4b13f3b","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","hash":"84d54afa70bf3e5c6c885b499b64f422da68e9f2bbfa8c41f6126de1b40b014b","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01HTq2ctZdyGXD8bnPMeW1xb","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && gh issue view 3 --comments; echo '------'; gh issue view 1; echo '------'; head -30 docs/agents/domain.md; ls app templates tests docs docs/adr 2>&1; wc -l app/*.py","description":"Read ticket T02, spec, and code layout"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}
{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","hash":"db666e8e618e7cc3876b2867c0be39aa70f3296fd2b7729682953685554bef44","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HTq2ctZdyGXD8bnPMeW1xb","type":"tool_result","content":"------\ntitle:\tSpec: KCFC web CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tiaishikb-rgb\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) is run by three Presidents and about eight Officers, and nearly everything is communicated by email to financeclub@kenyon.edu. The current Wix site shows no officers, no meeting time and no events, its Contact Us link goes back to the homepage, and its Resources headings have nothing under them, so a first-year or an alumnus can reasonably conclude the club is dead. Only one or two people can update it, there is no way to give Officers limited access, and nothing stops an unfinished stock pitch from going out under the club's name in front of William Blair alumni. When leadership changes there is no clean way to hand over or take away access.\n\nVocabulary below is defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Presidents** (3, Admin role): run the club, review everything, sign off on what goes public.\n- **Officers** (about 8, Editor role): contribute meeting announcements, pitch writeups and alumni call recaps. Not technical; an announcement must take under two minutes.\n- **Visitors** (never log in): prospective members (first-years and sophomores) asking \"what is this, do I need experience, when and where do you meet\"; current members looking for event details, the resume review form and the Analyst Program; alumni and recruiters (including William Blair) checking leadership and activity before an event or pitch review.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console on the Club laptop and a static public site. Presidents and Officers sign in with individual accounts. Officers write Posts and save Drafts; only Presidents publish, manage Pages, and manage Users. A Publish run turns everything Published into a static site on GitHub Pages. The first thing a Visitor sees is the next meeting. Nothing unreviewed reaches the public site, and an Officer who leaves loses access without anyone changing a shared password.\n\n## The 7 required capabilities, in KCFC's words\n\n1. **Login.** Presidents and Officers sign in and out with their Kenyon email and their own password. Passwords are stored hashed, never as text. A President sets the first password face to face, and resets lost passwords in person. Signed in on the shared Club laptop, a User is signed out after about 2 hours idle.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* (the three Presidents) can do everything. *Editor* (Officers) can write and edit only their own Posts, save them as Drafts and delete their own Drafts. An Editor cannot publish, cannot delete a Published Post, cannot touch any Page, and cannot see user management. These limits are enforced by the system itself, including when an Editor types a restricted address straight into the browser (the WordPress \"Editor can trash the About page\" problem from the field notes).\n3. **Posts.** One kind of Post (meeting announcement, pitch writeup, or alumni call recap), no categories. Each has a title, slug, Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author and timestamps, and can be created, read, updated and deleted under the role rules above. The slug is made from the title once and never changes when the title is edited; only an Admin can edit it. An Editor's edit to a Published Post turns it back into a Draft until a President republishes it. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n4. **Pages.** Lasting club information: Homepage, About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join (for prospective members), Recruiting (for current members: resume review form link, standing guides). Same fields as a Post, but only Admins may create, edit, or delete them. Published Pages appear in the public Navigation in an order an Admin sets. The Homepage opens with the **next-meeting line** (plain text such as \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\", updated by a President the night before), then the contact email, then the latest Posts.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated User counts), a one-click \"New Post\" button, and a \"pending changes\" banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live. A content list, newest first, filterable by status (All / Published / Draft, with counts) and type; Editors see only their own Posts. An editor with a side-by-side Preview of the sanitized Markdown, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** Presidents create Users, change Roles, and Deactivate Users. A Deactivated User cannot sign in, and an open session ends at their next action. Users are never deleted: when seniors graduate in May their old Posts keep their name but they cannot log in. A Deactivated User can be reactivated. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n7. **Public site and publish.** Visitors see only Published content. Markdown is sanitized (see below). Navigation is built from Published Pages plus a link to the Posts listing (newest first, title and date). Each Post shows a byline, \"By <name>, <date>\", never an email address; Pages show none. `cms publish` (Admin only, usually run right before a meeting) writes `site/` with relative paths only and deploys it to GitHub Pages. Marking an item Published has a \"Publish this?\" confirm. There is no change summary; a mistake is fixed by unpublishing and running it again.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a first-year, I want the next meeting's date, time and place at the very top of the homepage, so that I know when and where to show up.\n2. As a prospective member, I want a Join page saying what the club does and whether I need experience, so that I can decide whether to come.\n3. As a prospective member, I want the contact email on the homepage, so that I can ask a question.\n4. As a current member, I want a Recruiting page with the resume review form link, so that I can request a review without digging through email.\n5. As a current member, I want a list of Posts, newest first, so that I can find the latest announcement.\n6. As a current member, I want to read about the Analyst Program on its own page, so that I know what it involves.\n7. As an alumnus, I want a Leadership page, so that I know who runs the club before I speak at an event.\n8. As a recruiter or William Blair alumnus, I want to read reviewed pitch writeups and recaps, so that I can see the club's work, and I want to see only reviewed work.\n9. As a Visitor, I want links that keep working, so that a shared link to a Post is never dead.\n10. As a Visitor, I want to see an author's name but never their email address, so that student contact details stay private.\n11. As a Visitor, I want the site to work when served from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no page or link is broken.\n12. As an Officer, I want my own account, so that I never share a password.\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Kenyon email, so that it is easy to remember.\n14. As an Officer, I want to write a meeting announcement in under two minutes, so that updating the site is not a chore.\n15. As an Officer, I want to write in plain Markdown with a preview beside it, so that I can see what the Post will look like.\n16. As an Officer, I want to save my work as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n17. As an Officer, I want my Draft to stay private until a President publishes it, so that nothing goes public by accident.\n18. As an Officer, I want to see and edit only my own Posts, so that I do not break another team's pitch before the William Blair presentation.\n19. As an Officer, I want to delete my own abandoned Drafts, so that my list stays clean.\n20. As an Officer, I want to be told clearly when I cannot do something, so that I do not think the site is broken.\n21. As an Officer, I want a \"Draft, not Live\" label on my preview, so that I do not think members can already see it.\n22. As an Officer, I want to be signed out automatically on the shared laptop, so that the next person cannot use my account.\n23. As an Officer, I want my name on my Post after I graduate, so that my work keeps its credit.\n24. As a President, I want to review every Draft in one list, so that I can sign off before publishing.\n25. As a President, I want to see all Drafts filtered by status with counts, so that I know what still needs attention.\n26. As a President, I want to edit any Post, so that I can fix a pitch writeup before it goes out.\n27. As a President, I want an Officer's edit to a Published Post to turn it back to Draft, so that no unreviewed change goes out.\n28. As a President, I want a \"Publish this?\" confirm, so that I do not publish by mis-click.\n29. As a President, I want to unpublish a Post or Page, so that I can take down a mistake and rerun the publish.\n30. As a President, I want to delete a Post or Page after an \"are you sure?\" step, so that deletion is deliberate.\n31. As a President, I want only Presidents to edit or delete Leadership and Analyst Program (and every other Page), so that Officers cannot damage official pages.\n32. As a President, I want to set the order of Pages in Navigation, so that the menu reads sensibly.\n33. As a President, I want to edit the Homepage's next-meeting line, so that the first thing a first-year sees is current.\n34. As a President, I want a banner showing pending changes, so that I know the live site is behind.\n35. As a President, I want to run `cms publish` right before a meeting, so that the public site is up to date.\n36. As a President, I want to create accounts and set the first password in person, so that no email system is required.\n37. As a President, I want to reset a lost password in person, so that Officers are never locked out.\n38. As a President, I want to change a User's role, so that a new President can be made Admin at turnover.\n39. As a President, I want to deactivate an outgoing Officer, so that they can no longer sign in.\n40. As a President, I want a deactivated User to lose access immediately, even if signed in, so that handover is clean.\n41. As a President, I want to reactivate a User, so that a returning Officer does not need a new account.\n42. As a President, I want the system to refuse to deactivate the last active President or myself, so that the club cannot lock itself out.\n43. As a President, I want an Editor who types an Admin address into the browser to be refused, so that restrictions are real and not just hidden menu items.\n44. As a President, I want dashboard counts, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As a President, I want Posts to keep their author when the user is Deactivated, so that the archive stays accurate.\n46. As a President, I want Markdown to be sanitized everywhere it renders, so that nobody can inject a script into the club's site.\n47. As a President, I want the database file never to be committed, so that accounts and Drafts stay private.\n48. As a President, I want to hand the whole system to next year's Presidents without a shared password, so that continuity does not depend on one person.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture** follows ADR-001 (admin console local, public site static, explicit publish) and ADR-002 (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, argon2, no frontend framework). The dependency set in `pyproject.toml` is fixed; adding any dependency needs asking first.\n- **Roles:** exactly two, Admin and Editor. Permission checks live in one place on the server and every admin route goes through it, so direct URL access is refused as reliably as hidden menus. Editor-restricted requests return a refusal or redirect, never the page.\n- **Content model:** Post and Page share fields (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created and updated timestamps). A Post has no kind or category. Pages additionally have a navigation order. Status for a Page is Draft or Published like a Post.\n- **Slug rules:** generated from the title on first save, unique, immutable on title edit, editable only by an Admin, no redirects from old slugs. Navigation and the Posts listing use slugs, so links stay stable.\n- **Editing rules:** an Editor can read and change only Posts they authored; an Editor's save on a Published Post sets it to Draft. An Admin's save keeps its status. Marking Published is Admin-only and goes through a \"Publish this?\" confirm.\n- **Delete rules:** Admin can delete any Post or Page after a confirm step; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Unpublish (return to Draft) is separate from delete.\n- **Users:** email and argon2-hashed password; roles; active flag. Deactivating sets the flag; every request checks it, so an open session is refused at the next action. Users are never deleted. Guard rails: cannot deactivate or demote yourself, the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. First password is set by an Admin; no forced change at first sign-in; no email-based reset. Sessions are signed cookies with an idle timeout of about 2 hours.\n- **CSRF:** every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- **Sanitizing:** every rendered body goes through the sanitizer, both in the admin Preview and in the exported site. Scripts, event handlers such as `onerror`, iframes and `javascript:` links are stripped. Plain formatting, headings, lists and normal links stay. Raw HTML embeds are not supported and images are out of scope.\n- **Publish:** the exporter renders only Published Posts and Pages into `site/` using relative paths only (never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`): Homepage (with the next-meeting line and latest Posts), each Page, the Posts listing, each Post with its byline, and Navigation built from Published Pages in Admin-set order plus the Posts listing. Drafts never leave the database. `site/` is generated, never hand-edited. Deployment pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. \"Pending changes\" is the difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote.\n- **Console screens:** login/logout, dashboard (counts, New Post, pending changes banner), content list with status and type filters and counts, editor with side-by-side Preview, Page ordering, user management (Admin only).\n- **Seed and demo:** the existing seed script builds a demo database with one Admin and one Editor.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- A good test checks external behaviour only: what a signed-in role sees, can do, and is refused, and what ends up in the generated site. It does not assert on internal functions or database layout.\n- **Seam 1, the HTTP app,** through the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and logout, role permissions (including direct URL access), Post/Page CRUD, slug immutability, Editor-edit-reverts-to-Draft, own-Drafts-only, deactivation, last-Admin and self-deactivation guards, CSRF rejection, idle timeout, dashboard counts, filters and preview.\n- **Seam 2, the site export,** through the existing render function (`render_site(out_dir)`). It covers only-Published content, Drafts absent, sanitizer behaviour (scripts, `onerror`, iframes, `javascript:` links stripped; headings, lists, links kept), navigation order, byline text with no email, and no root-absolute `href`/`src`.\n- No new seams are needed; these two already exist and are the highest available. The existing front-door tests must keep passing.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (client and `render_site` tests), `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as` fixture, written so access-control tests are one line).\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly NOT building:\n\n- Comments\n- Image uploads (and any images or embeds in Markdown)\n- Categories or tags, or any kind of Post other than \"Post\"\n- Scheduled posts\n- Email newsletters, and any email sending (including password reset by email)\n- Member logins or any members-only content; Visitors never log in\n- A team or co-author field on Posts (team members are listed in the body text)\n- A calendar, an events system, or automatic next-meeting logic\n- Redirects from old slugs\n- A change summary or diff on the Publish run\n- A forced password change at first sign-in\n- In-app backup (the person with the Club laptop copies `cms.db` to the club Google Drive at the end of each semester, during board turnover)\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text (WYSIWYG) editors\n- Putting the admin console on the public internet\n- Search on the public site\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Handover of the system is a human process: Presidents create and deactivate accounts at board turnover, in person in Oden.\n- Spring pitch competition: three sector teams, each led by one President, present to William Blair alumni. Draft pitch writeups stay private until a President has reviewed them.\n- Post titles for pitches and recaps follow a club habit (\"Pitch: ...\", \"Recap: ...\"); the system does not enforce it.\n- `docs/agents/domain.md` still names `GLOSSARY.md`; the project glossary is `CONTEXT.md`, which this spec follows.\n\n------\n# Domain Docs & Glossary\n\nThis project uses a **single-context** layout: one shared glossary and one ADR collection at the repo root.\n\n## Files\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root: Project vocabulary. When new terms appear (entities, roles, workflows), add them here with definitions instead of using multiple names for the same thing.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: Architecture Decision Records. When a significant technical decision is made, document it as an ADR.\n\n## How skills use these\n\nEngineering skills (`to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `domain-modeling`) read from and write to these files:\n\n- **Reading the glossary**: Skills use `CONTEXT.md` to understand project vocabulary when writing specs, tickets, or analyzing code.\n- **Reading ADRs**: Skills consult `docs/adr/` to understand past decisions and constraints.\n- **Writing**: Skills may add entries to `CONTEXT.md` or suggest new ADRs when a decision needs recording.\n\n## Consumer rules\n\n- Whenever a ticket, spec, or ADR uses a term that could be ambiguous, **check `CONTEXT.md` first** and use the term as defined there.\n- If a better word appears, **update `CONTEXT.md`** rather than using both names.\n- If a technical decision is non-obvious or has implications, **consider an ADR** rather than only documenting it in code.\n\n## Single vs. multi-context\n\nThis repo is **single-context** (one app, one codebase, one glossary). If it becomes a monorepo with multiple packages, this should be updated to multi-context:\n\n- Upgrade `CONTEXT.md` to `CONTEXT-MAP.md` pointing to per-package glossaries.\n- Create `packages/<pkg>/docs/adr/` alongside the root `docs/adr/`.\n- Update this file to reflect the change.\napp:\n__init__.py\n__pycache__\nauth.py\ncli.py\ndb.py\nmain.py\npublish.py\nroutes\nseed.py\nsettings.py\ntemplating.py\nusers.py\n\ndocs:\nadr\nagents\nhandoff\nhandoffs\nmanual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\nmanual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md\nmp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nmp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\nmp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md\nprocess\nscreenshots\ntranscripts\n\ndocs/adr:\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\n\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntests:\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_ctx_guard.py\ntest_secret_key.py\ntest_t00.py\ntest_t01_login.py\ntest_usage_report.py\n       6 app/__init__.py\n      84 app/auth.py\n      60 app/cli.py\n      40 app/db.py\n      62 app/main.py\n      47 app/publish.py\n      23 app/seed.py\n      36 app/settings.py\n       9 app/templating.py\n      71 app/users.py\n     438 total","is_error":false}]}}

{"parentUuid":"b670b3ea-8895-4262-9edf-6c8b94b150fe","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"67b9a816-9212-46c1-99e5-1a81437be78f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HTq2ctZdyGXD8bnPMeW1xb","type":"tool_result","content":"------\ntitle:\tSpec: KCFC web CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tiaishikb-rgb\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) is run by three Presidents and about eight Officers, and nearly everything is communicated by email to financeclub@kenyon.edu. The current Wix site shows no officers, no meeting time and no events, its Contact Us link goes back to the homepage, and its Resources headings have nothing under them, so a first-year or an alumnus can reasonably conclude the club is dead. Only one or two people can update it, there is no way to give Officers limited access, and nothing stops an unfinished stock pitch from going out under the club's name in front of William Blair alumni. When leadership changes there is no clean way to hand over or take away access.\n\nVocabulary below is defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Presidents** (3, Admin role): run the club, review everything, sign off on what goes public.\n- **Officers** (about 8, Editor role): contribute meeting announcements, pitch writeups and alumni call recaps. Not technical; an announcement must take under two minutes.\n- **Visitors** (never log in): prospective members (first-years and sophomores) asking \"what is this, do I need experience, when and where do you meet\"; current members looking for event details, the resume review form and the Analyst Program; alumni and recruiters (including William Blair) checking leadership and activity before an event or pitch review.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console on the Club laptop and a static public site. Presidents and Officers sign in with individual accounts. Officers write Posts and save Drafts; only Presidents publish, manage Pages, and manage Users. A Publish run turns everything Published into a static site on GitHub Pages. The first thing a Visitor sees is the next meeting. Nothing unreviewed reaches the public site, and an Officer who leaves loses access without anyone changing a shared password.\n\n## The 7 required capabilities, in KCFC's words\n\n1. **Login.** Presidents and Officers sign in and out with their Kenyon email and their own password. Passwords are stored hashed, never as text. A President sets the first password face to face, and resets lost passwords in person. Signed in on the shared Club laptop, a User is signed out after about 2 hours idle.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* (the three Presidents) can do everything. *Editor* (Officers) can write and edit only their own Posts, save them as Drafts and delete their own Drafts. An Editor cannot publish, cannot delete a Published Post, cannot touch any Page, and cannot see user management. These limits are enforced by the system itself, including when an Editor types a restricted address straight into the browser (the WordPress \"Editor can trash the About page\" problem from the field notes).\n3. **Posts.** One kind of Post (meeting announcement, pitch writeup, or alumni call recap), no categories. Each has a title, slug, Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author and timestamps, and can be created, read, updated and deleted under the role rules above. The slug is made from the title once and never changes when the title is edited; only an Admin can edit it. An Editor's edit to a Published Post turns it back into a Draft until a President republishes it. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n4. **Pages.** Lasting club information: Homepage, About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join (for prospective members), Recruiting (for current members: resume review form link, standing guides). Same fields as a Post, but only Admins may create, edit, or delete them. Published Pages appear in the public Navigation in an order an Admin sets. The Homepage opens with the **next-meeting line** (plain text such as \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\", updated by a President the night before), then the contact email, then the latest Posts.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated User counts), a one-click \"New Post\" button, and a \"pending changes\" banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live. A content list, newest first, filterable by status (All / Published / Draft, with counts) and type; Editors see only their own Posts. An editor with a side-by-side Preview of the sanitized Markdown, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** Presidents create Users, change Roles, and Deactivate Users. A Deactivated User cannot sign in, and an open session ends at their next action. Users are never deleted: when seniors graduate in May their old Posts keep their name but they cannot log in. A Deactivated User can be reactivated. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n7. **Public site and publish.** Visitors see only Published content. Markdown is sanitized (see below). Navigation is built from Published Pages plus a link to the Posts listing (newest first, title and date). Each Post shows a byline, \"By <name>, <date>\", never an email address; Pages show none. `cms publish` (Admin only, usually run right before a meeting) writes `site/` with relative paths only and deploys it to GitHub Pages. Marking an item Published has a \"Publish this?\" confirm. There is no change summary; a mistake is fixed by unpublishing and running it again.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a first-year, I want the next meeting's date, time and place at the very top of the homepage, so that I know when and where to show up.\n2. As a prospective member, I want a Join page saying what the club does and whether I need experience, so that I can decide whether to come.\n3. As a prospective member, I want the contact email on the homepage, so that I can ask a question.\n4. As a current member, I want a Recruiting page with the resume review form link, so that I can request a review without digging through email.\n5. As a current member, I want a list of Posts, newest first, so that I can find the latest announcement.\n6. As a current member, I want to read about the Analyst Program on its own page, so that I know what it involves.\n7. As an alumnus, I want a Leadership page, so that I know who runs the club before I speak at an event.\n8. As a recruiter or William Blair alumnus, I want to read reviewed pitch writeups and recaps, so that I can see the club's work, and I want to see only reviewed work.\n9. As a Visitor, I want links that keep working, so that a shared link to a Post is never dead.\n10. As a Visitor, I want to see an author's name but never their email address, so that student contact details stay private.\n11. As a Visitor, I want the site to work when served from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no page or link is broken.\n12. As an Officer, I want my own account, so that I never share a password.\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Kenyon email, so that it is easy to remember.\n14. As an Officer, I want to write a meeting announcement in under two minutes, so that updating the site is not a chore.\n15. As an Officer, I want to write in plain Markdown with a preview beside it, so that I can see what the Post will look like.\n16. As an Officer, I want to save my work as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n17. As an Officer, I want my Draft to stay private until a President publishes it, so that nothing goes public by accident.\n18. As an Officer, I want to see and edit only my own Posts, so that I do not break another team's pitch before the William Blair presentation.\n19. As an Officer, I want to delete my own abandoned Drafts, so that my list stays clean.\n20. As an Officer, I want to be told clearly when I cannot do something, so that I do not think the site is broken.\n21. As an Officer, I want a \"Draft, not Live\" label on my preview, so that I do not think members can already see it.\n22. As an Officer, I want to be signed out automatically on the shared laptop, so that the next person cannot use my account.\n23. As an Officer, I want my name on my Post after I graduate, so that my work keeps its credit.\n24. As a President, I want to review every Draft in one list, so that I can sign off before publishing.\n25. As a President, I want to see all Drafts filtered by status with counts, so that I know what still needs attention.\n26. As a President, I want to edit any Post, so that I can fix a pitch writeup before it goes out.\n27. As a President, I want an Officer's edit to a Published Post to turn it back to Draft, so that no unreviewed change goes out.\n28. As a President, I want a \"Publish this?\" confirm, so that I do not publish by mis-click.\n29. As a President, I want to unpublish a Post or Page, so that I can take down a mistake and rerun the publish.\n30. As a President, I want to delete a Post or Page after an \"are you sure?\" step, so that deletion is deliberate.\n31. As a President, I want only Presidents to edit or delete Leadership and Analyst Program (and every other Page), so that Officers cannot damage official pages.\n32. As a President, I want to set the order of Pages in Navigation, so that the menu reads sensibly.\n33. As a President, I want to edit the Homepage's next-meeting line, so that the first thing a first-year sees is current.\n34. As a President, I want a banner showing pending changes, so that I know the live site is behind.\n35. As a President, I want to run `cms publish` right before a meeting, so that the public site is up to date.\n36. As a President, I want to create accounts and set the first password in person, so that no email system is required.\n37. As a President, I want to reset a lost password in person, so that Officers are never locked out.\n38. As a President, I want to change a User's role, so that a new President can be made Admin at turnover.\n39. As a President, I want to deactivate an outgoing Officer, so that they can no longer sign in.\n40. As a President, I want a deactivated User to lose access immediately, even if signed in, so that handover is clean.\n41. As a President, I want to reactivate a User, so that a returning Officer does not need a new account.\n42. As a President, I want the system to refuse to deactivate the last active President or myself, so that the club cannot lock itself out.\n43. As a President, I want an Editor who types an Admin address into the browser to be refused, so that restrictions are real and not just hidden menu items.\n44. As a President, I want dashboard counts, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As a President, I want Posts to keep their author when the user is Deactivated, so that the archive stays accurate.\n46. As a President, I want Markdown to be sanitized everywhere it renders, so that nobody can inject a script into the club's site.\n47. As a President, I want the database file never to be committed, so that accounts and Drafts stay private.\n48. As a President, I want to hand the whole system to next year's Presidents without a shared password, so that continuity does not depend on one person.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture** follows ADR-001 (admin console local, public site static, explicit publish) and ADR-002 (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, argon2, no frontend framework). The dependency set in `pyproject.toml` is fixed; adding any dependency needs asking first.\n- **Roles:** exactly two, Admin and Editor. Permission checks live in one place on the server and every admin route goes through it, so direct URL access is refused as reliably as hidden menus. Editor-restricted requests return a refusal or redirect, never the page.\n- **Content model:** Post and Page share fields (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created and updated timestamps). A Post has no kind or category. Pages additionally have a navigation order. Status for a Page is Draft or Published like a Post.\n- **Slug rules:** generated from the title on first save, unique, immutable on title edit, editable only by an Admin, no redirects from old slugs. Navigation and the Posts listing use slugs, so links stay stable.\n- **Editing rules:** an Editor can read and change only Posts they authored; an Editor's save on a Published Post sets it to Draft. An Admin's save keeps its status. Marking Published is Admin-only and goes through a \"Publish this?\" confirm.\n- **Delete rules:** Admin can delete any Post or Page after a confirm step; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Unpublish (return to Draft) is separate from delete.\n- **Users:** email and argon2-hashed password; roles; active flag. Deactivating sets the flag; every request checks it, so an open session is refused at the next action. Users are never deleted. Guard rails: cannot deactivate or demote yourself, the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. First password is set by an Admin; no forced change at first sign-in; no email-based reset. Sessions are signed cookies with an idle timeout of about 2 hours.\n- **CSRF:** every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- **Sanitizing:** every rendered body goes through the sanitizer, both in the admin Preview and in the exported site. Scripts, event handlers such as `onerror`, iframes and `javascript:` links are stripped. Plain formatting, headings, lists and normal links stay. Raw HTML embeds are not supported and images are out of scope.\n- **Publish:** the exporter renders only Published Posts and Pages into `site/` using relative paths only (never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`): Homepage (with the next-meeting line and latest Posts), each Page, the Posts listing, each Post with its byline, and Navigation built from Published Pages in Admin-set order plus the Posts listing. Drafts never leave the database. `site/` is generated, never hand-edited. Deployment pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. \"Pending changes\" is the difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote.\n- **Console screens:** login/logout, dashboard (counts, New Post, pending changes banner), content list with status and type filters and counts, editor with side-by-side Preview, Page ordering, user management (Admin only).\n- **Seed and demo:** the existing seed script builds a demo database with one Admin and one Editor.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- A good test checks external behaviour only: what a signed-in role sees, can do, and is refused, and what ends up in the generated site. It does not assert on internal functions or database layout.\n- **Seam 1, the HTTP app,** through the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and logout, role permissions (including direct URL access), Post/Page CRUD, slug immutability, Editor-edit-reverts-to-Draft, own-Drafts-only, deactivation, last-Admin and self-deactivation guards, CSRF rejection, idle timeout, dashboard counts, filters and preview.\n- **Seam 2, the site export,** through the existing render function (`render_site(out_dir)`). It covers only-Published content, Drafts absent, sanitizer behaviour (scripts, `onerror`, iframes, `javascript:` links stripped; headings, lists, links kept), navigation order, byline text with no email, and no root-absolute `href`/`src`.\n- No new seams are needed; these two already exist and are the highest available. The existing front-door tests must keep passing.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (client and `render_site` tests), `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as` fixture, written so access-control tests are one line).\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly NOT building:\n\n- Comments\n- Image uploads (and any images or embeds in Markdown)\n- Categories or tags, or any kind of Post other than \"Post\"\n- Scheduled posts\n- Email newsletters, and any email sending (including password reset by email)\n- Member logins or any members-only content; Visitors never log in\n- A team or co-author field on Posts (team members are listed in the body text)\n- A calendar, an events system, or automatic next-meeting logic\n- Redirects from old slugs\n- A change summary or diff on the Publish run\n- A forced password change at first sign-in\n- In-app backup (the person with the Club laptop copies `cms.db` to the club Google Drive at the end of each semester, during board turnover)\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text (WYSIWYG) editors\n- Putting the admin console on the public internet\n- Search on the public site\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Handover of the system is a human process: Presidents create and deactivate accounts at board turnover, in person in Oden.\n- Spring pitch competition: three sector teams, each led by one President, present to William Blair alumni. Draft pitch writeups stay private until a President has reviewed them.\n- Post titles for pitches and recaps follow a club habit (\"Pitch: ...\", \"Recap: ...\"); the system does not enforce it.\n- `docs/agents/domain.md` still names `GLOSSARY.md`; the project glossary is `CONTEXT.md`, which this spec follows.\n\n------\n# Domain Docs & Glossary\n\nThis project uses a **single-context** layout: one shared glossary and one ADR collection at the repo root.\n\n## Files\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root: Project vocabulary. When new terms appear (entities, roles, workflows), add them here with definitions instead of using multiple names for the same thing.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: Architecture Decision Records. When a significant technical decision is made, document it as an ADR.\n\n## How skills use these\n\nEngineering skills (`to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `domain-modeling`) read from and write to these files:\n\n- **Reading the glossary**: Skills use `CONTEXT.md` to understand project vocabulary when writing specs, tickets, or analyzing code.\n- **Reading ADRs**: Skills consult `docs/adr/` to understand past decisions and constraints.\n- **Writing**: Skills may add entries to `CONTEXT.md` or suggest new ADRs when a decision needs recording.\n\n## Consumer rules\n\n- Whenever a ticket, spec, or ADR uses a term that could be ambiguous, **check `CONTEXT.md` first** and use the term as defined there.\n- If a better word appears, **update `CONTEXT.md`** rather than using both names.\n- If a technical decision is non-obvious or has implications, **consider an ADR** rather than only documenting it in code.\n\n## Single vs. multi-context\n\nThis repo is **single-context** (one app, one codebase, one glossary). If it becomes a monorepo with multiple packages, this should be updated to multi-context:\n\n- Upgrade `CONTEXT.md` to `CONTEXT-MAP.md` pointing to per-package glossaries.\n- Create `packages/<pkg>/docs/adr/` alongside the root `docs/adr/`.\n- Update this file to reflect the change.\napp:\n__init__.py\n__pycache__\nauth.py\ncli.py\ndb.py\nmain.py\npublish.py\nroutes\nseed.py\nsettings.py\ntemplating.py\nusers.py\n\ndocs:\nadr\nagents\nhandoff\nhandoffs\nmanual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\nmanual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md\nmp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nmp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\nmp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md\nprocess\nscreenshots\ntranscripts\n\ndocs/adr:\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\n\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntests:\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_ctx_guard.py\ntest_secret_key.py\ntest_t00.py\ntest_t01_login.py\ntest_usage_report.py\n       6 app/__init__.py\n      84 app/auth.py\n      60 app/cli.py\n      40 app/db.py\n      62 app/main.py\n      47 app/publish.py\n      23 app/seed.py\n      36 app/settings.py\n       9 app/templating.py\n      71 app/users.py\n     438 total","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"e4a2e538-2f82-4a1f-bee5-560f3fa2f47c","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:35:23.354Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"------\ntitle:\tSpec: KCFC web CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tiaishikb-rgb\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) is run by three Presidents and about eight Officers, and nearly everything is communicated by email to financeclub@kenyon.edu. The current Wix site shows no officers, no meeting time and no events, its Contact Us link goes back to the homepage, and its Resources headings have nothing under them, so a first-year or an alumnus can reasonably conclude the club is dead. Only one or two people can update it, there is no way to give Officers limited access, and nothing stops an unfinished stock pitch from going out under the club's name in front of William Blair alumni. When leadership changes there is no clean way to hand over or take away access.\n\nVocabulary below is defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Presidents** (3, Admin role): run the club, review everything, sign off on what goes public.\n- **Officers** (about 8, Editor role): contribute meeting announcements, pitch writeups and alumni call recaps. Not technical; an announcement must take under two minutes.\n- **Visitors** (never log in): prospective members (first-years and sophomores) asking \"what is this, do I need experience, when and where do you meet\"; current members looking for event details, the resume review form and the Analyst Program; alumni and recruiters (including William Blair) checking leadership and activity before an event or pitch review.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console on the Club laptop and a static public site. Presidents and Officers sign in with individual accounts. Officers write Posts and save Drafts; only Presidents publish, manage Pages, and manage Users. A Publish run turns everything Published into a static site on GitHub Pages. The first thing a Visitor sees is the next meeting. Nothing unreviewed reaches the public site, and an Officer who leaves loses access without anyone changing a shared password.\n\n## The 7 required capabilities, in KCFC's words\n\n1. **Login.** Presidents and Officers sign in and out with their Kenyon email and their own password. Passwords are stored hashed, never as text. A President sets the first password face to face, and resets lost passwords in person. Signed in on the shared Club laptop, a User is signed out after about 2 hours idle.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* (the three Presidents) can do everything. *Editor* (Officers) can write and edit only their own Posts, save them as Drafts and delete their own Drafts. An Editor cannot publish, cannot delete a Published Post, cannot touch any Page, and cannot see user management. These limits are enforced by the system itself, including when an Editor types a restricted address straight into the browser (the WordPress \"Editor can trash the About page\" problem from the field notes).\n3. **Posts.** One kind of Post (meeting announcement, pitch writeup, or alumni call recap), no categories. Each has a title, slug, Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author and timestamps, and can be created, read, updated and deleted under the role rules above. The slug is made from the title once and never changes when the title is edited; only an Admin can edit it. An Editor's edit to a Published Post turns it back into a Draft until a President republishes it. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n4. **Pages.** Lasting club information: Homepage, About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join (for prospective members), Recruiting (for current members: resume review form link, standing guides). Same fields as a Post, but only Admins may create, edit, or delete them. Published Pages appear in the public Navigation in an order an Admin sets. The Homepage opens with the **next-meeting line** (plain text such as \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\", updated by a President the night before), then the contact email, then the latest Posts.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated User counts), a one-click \"New Post\" button, and a \"pending changes\" banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live. A content list, newest first, filterable by status (All / Published / Draft, with counts) and type; Editors see only their own Posts. An editor with a side-by-side Preview of the sanitized Markdown, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** Presidents create Users, change Roles, and Deactivate Users. A Deactivated User cannot sign in, and an open session ends at their next action. Users are never deleted: when seniors graduate in May their old Posts keep their name but they cannot log in. A Deactivated User can be reactivated. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n7. **Public site and publish.** Visitors see only Published content. Markdown is sanitized (see below). Navigation is built from Published Pages plus a link to the Posts listing (newest first, title and date). Each Post shows a byline, \"By <name>, <date>\", never an email address; Pages show none. `cms publish` (Admin only, usually run right before a meeting) writes `site/` with relative paths only and deploys it to GitHub Pages. Marking an item Published has a \"Publish this?\" confirm. There is no change summary; a mistake is fixed by unpublishing and running it again.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a first-year, I want the next meeting's date, time and place at the very top of the homepage, so that I know when and where to show up.\n2. As a prospective member, I want a Join page saying what the club does and whether I need experience, so that I can decide whether to come.\n3. As a prospective member, I want the contact email on the homepage, so that I can ask a question.\n4. As a current member, I want a Recruiting page with the resume review form link, so that I can request a review without digging through email.\n5. As a current member, I want a list of Posts, newest first, so that I can find the latest announcement.\n6. As a current member, I want to read about the Analyst Program on its own page, so that I know what it involves.\n7. As an alumnus, I want a Leadership page, so that I know who runs the club before I speak at an event.\n8. As a recruiter or William Blair alumnus, I want to read reviewed pitch writeups and recaps, so that I can see the club's work, and I want to see only reviewed work.\n9. As a Visitor, I want links that keep working, so that a shared link to a Post is never dead.\n10. As a Visitor, I want to see an author's name but never their email address, so that student contact details stay private.\n11. As a Visitor, I want the site to work when served from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no page or link is broken.\n12. As an Officer, I want my own account, so that I never share a password.\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Kenyon email, so that it is easy to remember.\n14. As an Officer, I want to write a meeting announcement in under two minutes, so that updating the site is not a chore.\n15. As an Officer, I want to write in plain Markdown with a preview beside it, so that I can see what the Post will look like.\n16. As an Officer, I want to save my work as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n17. As an Officer, I want my Draft to stay private until a President publishes it, so that nothing goes public by accident.\n18. As an Officer, I want to see and edit only my own Posts, so that I do not break another team's pitch before the William Blair presentation.\n19. As an Officer, I want to delete my own abandoned Drafts, so that my list stays clean.\n20. As an Officer, I want to be told clearly when I cannot do something, so that I do not think the site is broken.\n21. As an Officer, I want a \"Draft, not Live\" label on my preview, so that I do not think members can already see it.\n22. As an Officer, I want to be signed out automatically on the shared laptop, so that the next person cannot use my account.\n23. As an Officer, I want my name on my Post after I graduate, so that my work keeps its credit.\n24. As a President, I want to review every Draft in one list, so that I can sign off before publishing.\n25. As a President, I want to see all Drafts filtered by status with counts, so that I know what still needs attention.\n26. As a President, I want to edit any Post, so that I can fix a pitch writeup before it goes out.\n27. As a President, I want an Officer's edit to a Published Post to turn it back to Draft, so that no unreviewed change goes out.\n28. As a President, I want a \"Publish this?\" confirm, so that I do not publish by mis-click.\n29. As a President, I want to unpublish a Post or Page, so that I can take down a mistake and rerun the publish.\n30. As a President, I want to delete a Post or Page after an \"are you sure?\" step, so that deletion is deliberate.\n31. As a President, I want only Presidents to edit or delete Leadership and Analyst Program (and every other Page), so that Officers cannot damage official pages.\n32. As a President, I want to set the order of Pages in Navigation, so that the menu reads sensibly.\n33. As a President, I want to edit the Homepage's next-meeting line, so that the first thing a first-year sees is current.\n34. As a President, I want a banner showing pending changes, so that I know the live site is behind.\n35. As a President, I want to run `cms publish` right before a meeting, so that the public site is up to date.\n36. As a President, I want to create accounts and set the first password in person, so that no email system is required.\n37. As a President, I want to reset a lost password in person, so that Officers are never locked out.\n38. As a President, I want to change a User's role, so that a new President can be made Admin at turnover.\n39. As a President, I want to deactivate an outgoing Officer, so that they can no longer sign in.\n40. As a President, I want a deactivated User to lose access immediately, even if signed in, so that handover is clean.\n41. As a President, I want to reactivate a User, so that a returning Officer does not need a new account.\n42. As a President, I want the system to refuse to deactivate the last active President or myself, so that the club cannot lock itself out.\n43. As a President, I want an Editor who types an Admin address into the browser to be refused, so that restrictions are real and not just hidden menu items.\n44. As a President, I want dashboard counts, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As a President, I want Posts to keep their author when the user is Deactivated, so that the archive stays accurate.\n46. As a President, I want Markdown to be sanitized everywhere it renders, so that nobody can inject a script into the club's site.\n47. As a President, I want the database file never to be committed, so that accounts and Drafts stay private.\n48. As a President, I want to hand the whole system to next year's Presidents without a shared password, so that continuity does not depend on one person.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture** follows ADR-001 (admin console local, public site static, explicit publish) and ADR-002 (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, argon2, no frontend framework). The dependency set in `pyproject.toml` is fixed; adding any dependency needs asking first.\n- **Roles:** exactly two, Admin and Editor. Permission checks live in one place on the server and every admin route goes through it, so direct URL access is refused as reliably as hidden menus. Editor-restricted requests return a refusal or redirect, never the page.\n- **Content model:** Post and Page share fields (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created and updated timestamps). A Post has no kind or category. Pages additionally have a navigation order. Status for a Page is Draft or Published like a Post.\n- **Slug rules:** generated from the title on first save, unique, immutable on title edit, editable only by an Admin, no redirects from old slugs. Navigation and the Posts listing use slugs, so links stay stable.\n- **Editing rules:** an Editor can read and change only Posts they authored; an Editor's save on a Published Post sets it to Draft. An Admin's save keeps its status. Marking Published is Admin-only and goes through a \"Publish this?\" confirm.\n- **Delete rules:** Admin can delete any Post or Page after a confirm step; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Unpublish (return to Draft) is separate from delete.\n- **Users:** email and argon2-hashed password; roles; active flag. Deactivating sets the flag; every request checks it, so an open session is refused at the next action. Users are never deleted. Guard rails: cannot deactivate or demote yourself, the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. First password is set by an Admin; no forced change at first sign-in; no email-based reset. Sessions are signed cookies with an idle timeout of about 2 hours.\n- **CSRF:** every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- **Sanitizing:** every rendered body goes through the sanitizer, both in the admin Preview and in the exported site. Scripts, event handlers such as `onerror`, iframes and `javascript:` links are stripped. Plain formatting, headings, lists and normal links stay. Raw HTML embeds are not supported and images are out of scope.\n- **Publish:** the exporter renders only Published Posts and Pages into `site/` using relative paths only (never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`): Homepage (with the next-meeting line and latest Posts), each Page, the Posts listing, each Post with its byline, and Navigation built from Published Pages in Admin-set order plus the Posts listing. Drafts never leave the database. `site/` is generated, never hand-edited. Deployment pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. \"Pending changes\" is the difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote.\n- **Console screens:** login/logout, dashboard (counts, New Post, pending changes banner), content list with status and type filters and counts, editor with side-by-side Preview, Page ordering, user management (Admin only).\n- **Seed and demo:** the existing seed script builds a demo database with one Admin and one Editor.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- A good test checks external behaviour only: what a signed-in role sees, can do, and is refused, and what ends up in the generated site. It does not assert on internal functions or database layout.\n- **Seam 1, the HTTP app,** through the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and logout, role permissions (including direct URL access), Post/Page CRUD, slug immutability, Editor-edit-reverts-to-Draft, own-Drafts-only, deactivation, last-Admin and self-deactivation guards, CSRF rejection, idle timeout, dashboard counts, filters and preview.\n- **Seam 2, the site export,** through the existing render function (`render_site(out_dir)`). It covers only-Published content, Drafts absent, sanitizer behaviour (scripts, `onerror`, iframes, `javascript:` links stripped; headings, lists, links kept), navigation order, byline text with no email, and no root-absolute `href`/`src`.\n- No new seams are needed; these two already exist and are the highest available. The existing front-door tests must keep passing.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (client and `render_site` tests), `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as` fixture, written so access-control tests are one line).\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly NOT building:\n\n- Comments\n- Image uploads (and any images or embeds in Markdown)\n- Categories or tags, or any kind of Post other than \"Post\"\n- Scheduled posts\n- Email newsletters, and any email sending (including password reset by email)\n- Member logins or any members-only content; Visitors never log in\n- A team or co-author field on Posts (team members are listed in the body text)\n- A calendar, an events system, or automatic next-meeting logic\n- Redirects from old slugs\n- A change summary or diff on the Publish run\n- A forced password change at first sign-in\n- In-app backup (the person with the Club laptop copies `cms.db` to the club Google Drive at the end of each semester, during board turnover)\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text (WYSIWYG) editors\n- Putting the admin console on the public internet\n- Search on the public site\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Handover of the system is a human process: Presidents create and deactivate accounts at board turnover, in person in Oden.\n- Spring pitch competition: three sector teams, each led by one President, present to William Blair alumni. Draft pitch writeups stay private until a President has reviewed them.\n- Post titles for pitches and recaps follow a club habit (\"Pitch: ...\", \"Recap: ...\"); the system does not enforce it.\n- `docs/agents/domain.md` still names `GLOSSARY.md`; the project glossary is `CONTEXT.md`, which this spec follows.\n\n------\n# Domain Docs & Glossary\n\nThis project uses a **single-context** layout: one shared glossary and one ADR collection at the repo root.\n\n## Files\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root: Project vocabulary. When new terms appear (entities, roles, workflows), add them here with definitions instead of using multiple names for the same thing.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: Architecture Decision Records. If it becomes a monorepo with multiple packages, this should be updated to multi-context:\n\n- Upgrade `CONTEXT.md` to `CONTEXT-MAP.md` pointing to per-package glossaries.\n- Create `packages/<pkg>/docs/adr/` alongside the root `docs/adr/`.\n- Update this file to reflect the change.\napp:\n__init__.py\n__pycache__\nauth.py\ncli.py\ndb.py\nmain.py\npublish.py\nroutes\nseed.py\nsettings.py\ntemplating.py\nusers.py\n\ndocs:\nadr\nagents\nhandoff\nhandoffs\nmanual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\nmanual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md\nmp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nmp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\nmp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md\nprocess\nscreenshots\ntranscripts\n\ndocs/adr:\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\n\ntemplates:\nadmin\nbase.html\npublic\n\ntests:\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_ctx_guard.py\ntest_secret_key.py\ntest_t00.py\ntest_t01_login.py\ntest_usage_report.py\n       6 app/__init__.py\n      84 app/auth.py\n      60 app/cli.py\n      40 app/db.py\n      62 app/main.py\n      47 app/publish.py\n      23 app/seed.py\n      36 app/settings.py\n       9 app/templating.py\n      71 app/users.py\n     438 total","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b670b3ea-8895-4262-9edf-6c8b94b150fe","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"455b284b-7033-4640-9e05-1b056df536d6","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

New Posts are always Drafts. An Editor sees and edits only their own Posts, and a direct URL to someone else's Post is refused.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n- [ ] An Officer creates a Post with title and Markdown body; it is saved as a Draft with the Officer as author and timestamps set\n- [ ] The slug is generated from the title once, made unique, and does not change when the title is edited\n- [ ] An Editor cannot edit the slug field (Admin-only; covered in T03)\n- [ ] The Preview renders the Markdown through the sanitizer (script, onerror, iframe and javascript: links stripped; headings, lists, links kept) and shows \"Draft, not Live\"\n- [ ] An Officer sees only their own Posts in the list; requesting another Officer's Post by URL is refused (403 or redirect)\n- [ ] An Officer can delete their own Draft after an \"are you sure?\" step\n- [ ] A President can open and edit any Post\n- [ ] Creating an announcement takes one form and one click (target: under two minutes)\n- [ ] Tests cover the above via `client_as`; every form has a CSRF token\n- [ ] Commit starts \"T02:\" and ends \"Closes #<this issue number>\"; `/code-review` findings are posted on this issue first\n\nBlocked by: #2","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"970ccc9f-16e0-4ad2-8c04-77a4e1ffee8f","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:35:25.917Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"T02: Officers write and edit their own Post drafts\nPart of spec #1. Vocabulary: `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## What to build\nA vertical slice for **Posts as an Officer**: a Post table (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created/updated timestamps); routes to create, list (own only), edit and delete-own-Draft; a post editor template with a side-by-side **Preview** that renders sanitized Markdown, labelled \"Draft, not Live\"; automatic **Slug** from the title on first save (unique, unchanged when the title is edited).
